::: {.callout-note}
Lake Rotorua has a single surface outflow, the Ōhau Channel, which is controlled by a
weir with removable stoplogs. GLM cannot represent a two-level crest with stoplogs, so we
replace it with **one equivalent crest** (elevation, width, and a dimensionless factor)
fitted to the gauged lake level and channel discharge. This page documents the physical
weir, the data used, and how the GLM parameters are derived.
:::

```{r setup}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")

source(here::here("R", "plot_rotorua_weir_profile.R"))
source(here::here("R", "est_glm_weir_params.R"))
source(here::here("R", "rotorua_weir_flow.R"))

store <- here::here("_targets")
flow_level <- targets::tar_read(ohau_flow_level, store = store)
weir_fit <- targets::tar_read(glm_weir_params, store = store)
weir_params <- targets::tar_read(weir_params, store = store)

# Physical weir geometry (m)
channel_width_m <- 26
lower_width_m <- 4.6
upper_width_m <- channel_width_m - lower_width_m
lower_crest_m <- 278.166
upper_crest_m <- 279.316
stoplog_height_m <- 0.270
cd <- 0.565

levels_ref <- c(
  "Install trigger" = 279.776,
  "Remove trigger" = 279.966,
  "Consented maximum" = 280.076
)

# GLM fit
crest_elev <- weir_fit$crest_elev
crest_factor <- weir_fit$crest_factor
```

## 1. The physical weir

The weir spans the **26 m wide** Ōhau Channel. It has two crest levels:

- a narrow, deep **lower crest** (4.6 m wide, 278.166 m) in the centre of the channel, and
- a higher **upper crest** (279.316 m) across the remaining 21.4 m.

Up to three **stoplogs**, each 0.270 m high, can be stacked on the lower crest to raise the
low-flow control level. Their installation and removal are tied to lake-level triggers.

```{r weir-table}
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~Item, ~Value, ~Unit,
  "Channel width", channel_width_m, "m",
  "Lower crest width", lower_width_m, "m",
  "Upper crest width (total, both sides)", upper_width_m, "m",
  "Lower crest elevation", lower_crest_m, "m a.s.l.",
  "Upper crest elevation", upper_crest_m, "m a.s.l.",
  "Stoplog height (each)", stoplog_height_m, "m",
  "Number of stoplogs", NA, "0 to 3",
  "Lower crest with 3 stoplogs", lower_crest_m + 3 * stoplog_height_m, "m a.s.l.",
  "Stoplog install trigger", levels_ref[["Install trigger"]], "m a.s.l.",
  "Stoplog remove trigger", levels_ref[["Remove trigger"]], "m a.s.l.",
  "Consented maximum lake level", levels_ref[["Consented maximum"]], "m a.s.l."
) |>
  kbl(digits = 3) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Weir diagram

The across-channel profile (looking downstream) is shown below for 0 to 3 stoplogs. Stoplogs
stack on the lower crest; with three installed the lower section (`r round(lower_crest_m + 3 * stoplog_height_m, 3)` m)
is almost level with the upper crest (`r upper_crest_m` m). Horizontal lines are the
lake-level references.

```{r weir-profile}
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Across-channel weir crest profile with 0–3 stoplogs. Schematic."
plot_rotorua_weir_profile()
```

## 2. Observed lake level and outflow

Lake level (`Lake Level.Moturiki`) and channel discharge (`Discharge.Primary`) at the Ōhau
Channel site (BoPRC site FL150407) are joined on timestamp.

```{r data-summary}
#| echo: false
fl <- flow_level |> filter(is.finite(level), is.finite(flow))
tibble::tibble(
  Variable = c("Records with both level and flow", "Start", "End",
               "Level range (m)", "Flow range (m³/s)", "Median flow (m³/s)"),
  Value = c(
    format(nrow(fl), big.mark = ","),
    format(min(fl$Date), "%Y-%m-%d"),
    format(max(fl$Date), "%Y-%m-%d"),
    paste(round(range(fl$level), 2), collapse = " – "),
    paste(round(range(fl$flow), 1), collapse = " – "),
    round(median(fl$flow), 1)
  )
) |>
  kbl() |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

```{r timeseries}
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Daily mean lake level (top) and Ōhau Channel discharge (bottom), with weir elevations and stoplog triggers marked."
daily <- fl |>
  mutate(day = as.Date(Date)) |>
  group_by(day) |>
  summarise(level = mean(level), flow = mean(flow), .groups = "drop")

p_lvl <- ggplot(daily, aes(day, level)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = upper_crest_m, colour = "grey50", linetype = "solid") +
  geom_hline(
    data = tibble::enframe(levels_ref, "reference", "y"),
    aes(yintercept = y, colour = reference, linetype = reference)
  ) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Install trigger" = "#0072B2",
                                 "Remove trigger" = "#D55E00",
                                 "Consented maximum" = "#009E73"), name = NULL) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("Install trigger" = "dotted",
                                   "Remove trigger" = "dashed",
                                   "Consented maximum" = "solid"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Lake level (m a.s.l.)")

p_flow <- ggplot(daily, aes(day, flow)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.3, colour = "#0072B2") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Discharge (m³/s)")

patchwork::wrap_plots(p_lvl, p_flow, ncol = 1)
```

Every observation sits above the upper crest, so flow is always passing over the whole
weir. The stoplogs only change how much of the flow goes over the lower versus upper section.

### Level–flow relationship

```{r level-flow}
#| fig-cap: "Gauged discharge against lake level, coloured by year."
fl |>
  mutate(year = lubridate::year(Date)) |>
  slice_sample(n = min(60000, nrow(fl))) |>
  ggplot(aes(level, flow, colour = year)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.5) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c() +
  labs(x = "Lake level (m a.s.l.)", y = "Discharge (m³/s)", colour = "Year")
```

The cloud has spread at any given level: stoplog configuration, vegetation and gauge
hysteresis all change the effective rating over time. A single curve can only capture the
central tendency.

## 3. Physical weir rating curves

For each stoplog count the discharge is the sum of the flow over the lower and the upper
sections, each treated as a broad-crested rectangular weir at critical flow:

$$
Q = 1.705\, C_d \Big[\, b_{low}\,(h - z_{low})_+^{3/2} + b_{up}\,(h - z_{up})_+^{3/2} \Big]
$$

where $1.705 = \tfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{2g/3}$ is the critical-flow broad-crested weir
coefficient (SI units), $h$ is lake level, $z_{low} = 278.166 + n \times 0.270$ is the
lower crest with $n$ stoplogs, $z_{up} = 279.316$, $b_{low} = 4.6$ m, $b_{up} = 21.4$ m,
and $C_d =$ `r cd` is an empirical discharge coefficient. This is
`rotorua_weir_flow()` / `generate_rotorua_weir_curves()` in
[R/rotorua_weir_flow.R](../R/rotorua_weir_flow.R), as used in `compare_rating_curve.R`.

```{r curves}
lvl_seq <- seq(upper_crest_m, max(fl$level, na.rm = TRUE) + 0.05, by = 0.01)
curves <- generate_rotorua_weir_curves(
  level_range_m = range(lvl_seq), by_m = 0.01, cd = cd
)
```

```{r curves-plot}
#| fig-cap: "Gauged level–flow data (grey) with the physical weir rating curve for 0–3 stoplogs."
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = slice_sample(fl, n = min(40000, nrow(fl))),
             aes(level, flow), size = 0.3, alpha = 0.3, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(data = curves,
            aes(level_m, flow_m3s, colour = factor(n_stoplogs)), linewidth = 0.9) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "Stoplogs") +
  labs(x = "Lake level (m a.s.l.)", y = "Discharge (m³/s)")
```

```{r curves-by-year}
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-cap: "Same comparison split by year."
fl |>
  mutate(year = factor(lubridate::year(Date))) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  slice_sample(n = 3000) |>
  ungroup() |>
  ggplot(aes(level, flow)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(data = curves, aes(level_m, flow_m3s, colour = factor(n_stoplogs))) +
  facet_wrap(~year) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "Stoplogs") +
  labs(x = "Lake level (m a.s.l.)", y = "Discharge (m³/s)")
```

## 4. How GLM represents the outflow

GLM treats the lake outflow as a single rectangular broad-crested weir. When the water
level $h$ is above the crest, outflow is

$$
Q = \tfrac{2}{3}\, f_c \sqrt{2g}\; w_c\, (h - z_c)_+^{3/2}
$$

with three parameters in the `.nml`:

| GLM parameter | Namelist entry | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Crest elevation $z_c$ | `&morphometry` `crest_elev` | Height of the single equivalent crest (m a.s.l.) |
| Crest width $w_c$ | `&outflow` `crest_width` | Width of the weir (m) |
| Crest factor $f_c$ | `&outflow` `crest_factor` | Dimensionless discharge coefficient, a free scaling on flow |

Because the physical weir has two crest levels and a stoplog configuration that changes
through time, the GLM parameters are **not** measured, they are fitted so that the single
crest reproduces the gauged rating.

### Choices

- **Crest width** is fixed at the full channel width, **26 m** (`ohau_weir_width` target),
  so $w_c$ is not fitted and the factor absorbs the loss in effective width.
- **Crest elevation** and **crest factor** are fitted by least squares on all paired
  observations (`flow >= 0`, finite level and flow).
- For any trial crest elevation $z_c$ the best factor has a closed form. With
  $q_i = \tfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{2g}\; w_c (h_i - z_c)_+^{3/2}$,

$$
f_c(z_c) = \frac{\sum q_i Q_i}{\sum q_i^2}
$$

  and `optimize()` then searches $z_c$ between the lower and upper physical crests
  (278.166–279.316 m) to minimise the sum of squared errors.

This is implemented in `est_glm_weir_params()` ([R/est_glm_weir_params.R](../R/est_glm_weir_params.R)),
run by the `glm_weir_params` target, and written to the model by `format_weir_params()`.

```{r fit-result}
#| echo: false
tibble::tribble(
  ~Parameter, ~`GLM name`, ~Value, ~`How set`,
  "Crest elevation", "morphometry/crest_elev", round(crest_elev, 4), "Fitted",
  "Crest width", "outflow/crest_width", channel_width_m, "Fixed (channel width)",
  "Crest factor", "outflow/crest_factor", round(crest_factor, 4), "Fitted (closed form)",
  "Number of outlets", "outflow/num_outlet", 0, "Fixed (surface weir only)"
) |>
  kbl() |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Fit against observations

```{r fit-plot}
#| fig-cap: "Gauged discharge (points) and the GLM single-crest rating (red)."
fl$est_flow <- glm_weir_outflow(fl$level, crest_factor, crest_elev, channel_width_m)

rating <- tibble::tibble(level = lvl_seq) |>
  mutate(flow = glm_weir_outflow(level, crest_factor, crest_elev, channel_width_m))

ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = slice_sample(fl, n = min(40000, nrow(fl))),
             aes(level, flow), size = 0.3, alpha = 0.3, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(data = rating, aes(level, flow), colour = "red", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = crest_elev, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D55E00") +
  labs(x = "Lake level (m a.s.l.)", y = "Discharge (m³/s)")
```

```{r fit-stats}
#| echo: false
resid <- fl$flow - fl$est_flow
tibble::tibble(
  Metric = c("RMSE (m³/s)", "Bias, mean(obs − est) (m³/s)", "R²",
             "Sum(estimated) / Sum(observed)"),
  Value = c(
    sqrt(mean(resid^2)),
    mean(resid),
    cor(fl$flow, fl$est_flow)^2,
    sum(fl$est_flow) / sum(fl$flow)
  )
) |>
  kbl(digits = 3) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

### Equivalent crest versus the real weir

The fitted crest (`r round(crest_elev, 3)` m) falls between the lower crest and the upper
crest. This is expected: it is a flow-weighted compromise between a narrow section that
passes water at low heads and a wide, higher section that dominates at high heads.

```{r glm-vs-actual}
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Actual weir (0 and 2 stoplogs) against the GLM single-crest approximation (dashed)."
patchwork::wrap_plots(
  plot_rotorua_glm_weir_comparison(crest_elev, crest_factor, n_stoplogs = 0),
  plot_rotorua_glm_weir_comparison(crest_elev, crest_factor, n_stoplogs = 2),
  ncol = 1, guides = "collect"
)
```

The crest factor does not move the drawn crest. It scales flow. Note the GLM equation
uses $\tfrac{2}{3}\sqrt{2g} = `r round((2/3)*sqrt(2*9.81), 3)`$ as its base coefficient,
whereas the physical curves use $1.705\,C_d$ = `r round(1.705 * cd, 3)`. Per metre of
crest width at the same head, the fitted GLM coefficient is
$`r round((2/3)*sqrt(2*9.81), 3)` \times `r round(crest_factor, 3)` = `r round((2/3)*sqrt(2*9.81)*crest_factor, 3)`$,
of similar magnitude to the physical `r round(1.705 * cd, 3)`. The GLM crest sits lower
than the upper crest, so it compensates for the physical weir's higher crest with a
slightly higher unit coefficient over the full 26 m.

### Rating comparison: physical vs GLM

```{r glm-vs-physical}
#| fig-cap: "GLM equivalent rating compared with the physical weir rating for 0–3 stoplogs."
ggplot() +
  geom_line(data = curves, aes(level_m, flow_m3s, colour = factor(n_stoplogs)),
            linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_line(data = rating, aes(level, flow, linetype = "GLM single crest"),
            colour = "red", linewidth = 1.1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(name = "Physical weir\nstoplogs") +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c("GLM single crest" = "dashed"), name = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Lake level (m a.s.l.)", y = "Discharge (m³/s)")
```

## 5. Writing the parameters into GLM

`format_weir_params()` returns the table that the calibration workflow applies to
`glm4.nml`. The `min` and `max` columns are the parameter bounds for calibration: ±0.2 m
on the crest elevation, and −0.1 / +0.2 on the factor.

```{r nml-params}
#| echo: false
weir_params |>
  select(name, value, min, max) |>
  kbl(digits = 4) |>
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "condensed"), full_width = FALSE)
```

Resulting namelist entries:

```
&morphometry
   crest_elev   = <crest_elev>      ! fitted
/
&outflow
   num_outlet   = 0                 ! surface weir only; no submerged outlet
   crest_width  = 26.0              ! channel width
   crest_factor = <crest_factor>    ! fitted
/
```

### Caveats

- **One curve for all stoplog states.** The fit pools all years and stoplog
  configurations; stoplog history is not used. The GLM rating is a compromise, so it will
  overpredict flow in periods when logs are in and underpredict when they are out
  (the scatter at a given level in the figure above shows this spread).
- **Pooled fit weights high flows.** Least squares on flow is driven by the large
  discharges, so the low-head end of the rating is less well matched.
- **Fitted crest is an effective value.** It should not be compared with a surveyed crest
  level, and the bounds for calibration (±0.2 m) are deliberately narrow around it.
- **Datum.** Both level and crest elevations are in Moturiki datum, which must match the
  datum of the lake hypsograph used in GLM (see the `crest_elev` row in the config notes).
